items.expected-result: register_decision_task then record_decision on a registered scratch project. A record without status is proposed, status=accepted is accepted, and an empty required field is refused as invalid-argument. Resending the same sessionId+requestId returns replayed=true with the same decisionId and revision; judge 'no duplicate' by the export counts, not by the replay flag alone. (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)
items.evidence: register task: replayed=false projectRevision 1; same pair: replayed=true projectRevision 1. record A (no status): status proposed, version 1, revision 2; replay same requestId: replayed=true, same decisionId 01a1cad0-8aa0-..., revision 2. record B status=accepted: status accepted. outcome='': isError invalid-argument: Parameter "outcome" ... must not be null or whitespace. Later export --all counts: decisions 4, versions 7 (A x4, B, C, CLI x1)
items.observed-result: Default status, explicit status, the refusal and the idempotent replay all hold. The export counts show the replay did not write a second decision.

items.expected-result: Each write guard must be seen refusing: amend with a stale expectedVersion -> decision-conflict naming currentVersion; accepted->proposed -> decision-invalid-transition; link_decisions with a stale expectedProjectRevision -> decision-conflict; amending a superseded decision -> decision-invalid-transition. Pair each refusal with the same call succeeding on fresh values. (ADR-0142, docs/how-to/record-project-decisions.md)

items.observed-result: Read-only mode refuses writes on both surfaces, writes nothing, keeps reads working and survives a restart. Driver note: the after-restart step was run a second time after rw was restored, and that run recorded one extra decision titled 'ro'. The driver repeated its own write; the refusal did not leak. The deciding evidence is the revision check made while ro (9 before, 9 after).
